reason: The bone-lineage environment appears to direct stem-cell descendants toward the bone-forming cells described in the chapter.
expectation: The cell population will begin developing along the bone lineage.

effect: The lineage now includes matrix-producing osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, ready for the mature-bone construction.
reaction: The distinction between bone-forming and embedded cells is useful.
reason: The mineral appears suited to reinforcing the arm's collagen framework.
expectation: The mineral will strengthen the collagen framework to form bone.

effect: The framework now contains mineral, illustrating how collagen and mineral contribute different mechanical properties.
reaction: The contrast between toughness and compression resistance is helpful.
reason: The chapter calls for living cells in the mature bone, so the bone cells should join the mineralised framework.
expectation: The framework will gain living bone cells, including embedded osteocytes.

effect: The mineralised bones now contain connected living cells; the remaining vessels may supply them.
reaction: The tiny channels make the cells' connections through hard matrix clearer.
reason: Blood vessels are the remaining component most directly associated with supporting living bone.
expectation: The bones will gain a blood supply that supports their living cells.

effect: The arm bones now have vessels supplying nutrients to their embedded cells; the next task is assembling the elbow.
reaction: The cutaway usefully distinguishes nutrients leaving the vessels from blood cells remaining inside.
reason: Articular cartilage should cover the bone ends where they meet at the elbow.
expectation: Cartilage will cap the joint surfaces of the arm bones.

effect: The elbow-facing bone surfaces now have cartilage caps that can slide against one another.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: The synovial capsule appears to enclose the cartilage-covered joint and its fluid.
expectation: The capsule will surround the elbow joint, leaving fluid around its moving surfaces.

effect: The elbow is now enclosed by a fluid-containing capsule; the remaining ligaments can support it.
reaction: The lining's role in supplying lubricating fluid is clear.
reason: The elbow ligaments span the joint and should help support the movable skeleton.
expectation: The ligaments will stabilize the elbow while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments completed the supported, movable arm skeleton; the arrows distinguish elbow bending from resistance to sideways movement.
reaction: The final cutaway ties the joint components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral to the collagen framework was most worthwhile: the planned inset and explanation connect the two materials to toughness and resistance to compression.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the capsule was clear but relatively predictable after the cartilage; its main new detail was that the lining supplies fluid.

surprise.text: The bone-cell lineage showed matrix-producing osteoblasts becoming embedded osteocytes, with processes connecting through tiny channels. That made living bone more than a mineral framework.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt purposeless, though placing already-developed bone cells into a separately mineralised framework is a construction shortcut rather than the lineage sequence shown earlier.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing another structure assembled with similarly clear links between its materials and function, although the sequence here was quite predictable.
